Good evening. Sorry for getting your clean floor wet.
Do not worry at all! You must be Javier.

Hot soup? After that cold walk in the rain, that sounds wonderful.
Sir, before going upstairs, I owe you an honest apology.

We accidentally booked two guests into room seven tonight.
Oh dear... in this rain? Every hotel near the station looked full.
Please do not worry! We prepared our quiet third-floor attic room just for you.
An attic room? May I see it first?

Hot soup? After that cold walk in the rain, that sounds wonderful.

Hot soup? After that cold walk in the rain, that sounds wonderful.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.trans: There are four tables inside.
I will be back in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Resguárdese de la lluvia = step out of the rain.

examples.text: El porche nos resguarda del viento.
examples.trans: The porch shelters us from the wind.

examples.text: Se resguardaron bajo el toldo verde.
examples.trans: They sheltered under the green awning.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Bajo la lluvia = in the rain.

examples.text: La lluvia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The rain is very important here.
We talk about the rain.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Everyday polite apology or attention-getter.

examples.text: Perdón por llegar cinco minutos tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving five minutes late.
Pardon? Could you repeat the number?

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: La lluvia moja los adoquines grises.
examples.trans: The rain wets the grey cobblestones.

examples.text: Perdón por mojar la entrada con el paraguas.
examples.trans: Sorry for wetting the entrance with my umbrella.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

soler.gloss: to usually do; to tend to (soler + infinitive)

meanings.en: to usually do; to tend to (soler + infinitive)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suelo, suele, suelen) used in present/imperfect + infinitive.

examples.text: Suelo tomar café a las ocho.
examples.trans: I usually have coffee at eight.

examples.text: Estos muros suelen guardar el fresco.
examples.trans: These walls usually keep the air cool.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

nada.gloss: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)

meanings.en: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)
meanings.note: No pasa nada = no problem; nada de... = no ... at all.

examples.trans: Easy now, there is no problem at all.
There is no butter left at all.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

meanings.note: With a noun object (le debo la verdad), means 'to owe'; before an infinitive, means 'should / ought to'.

examples.text: Le debo diez euros de cambio.
examples.trans: I owe you ten euros in change.
Everything works as it should.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Pairs naturally with preterite tense.

examples.trans: Yesterday we fixed the boiler.

examples.text: Llegué a Valencia ayer por la tarde.
examples.trans: I arrived in Valencia yesterday afternoon.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Reservo una mesa tranquila para tres.
examples.trans: I book a quiet table for three.

examples.text: Reservamos la habitación hace un mes.
examples.trans: We booked the room a month ago.

meanings.note: Por teléfono = by phone / on the phone.

examples.trans: The telephone is here.

examples.text: Vemos los teléfonos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the telephones from the door.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Clean bath or hand towel.

examples.trans: The towel is here.

examples.text: Vemos las toallas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the towels from the door.

meanings.note: Toallas secas = dry towels.

examples.trans: It is a dry piece.

examples.text: ¡Javier lo dejó ahí cuando cogió la toalla seca!
examples.trans: Javier set it down there when he took the dry towel!

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Warm outer coat worn in cold or rainy weather.

examples.trans: The coat is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abrigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coats from the door.

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

meanings.note: Hecho una sopa = soaked through.

examples.trans: The soup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sopas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the soups from the door.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.
What do we do after that?

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: A short journey on foot, or a wide tree-lined street.

examples.text: Dieron un paseo largo por la tarde.
examples.trans: They took a long walk in the afternoon.
It is a very beautiful walk.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el frío), means 'the cold'.

examples.trans: It is a cold piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun; por eso = that is why.

examples.trans: That is why I brought two umbrellas.
What does that mean exactly?

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: ¡Qué maravilla! = How wonderful!

examples.trans: The wonder is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maravillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wonders from the door.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Disculpe (usted) / Disculpa (tú) is polite 'excuse me'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Nos disculpamos por el pequeño retraso.
examples.trans: We apologized for the brief delay.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.trans: It is a honest piece.

examples.text: Señor, antes de subir, le debo una disculpa sincera.
examples.trans: Sir, before going upstairs, I owe you an honest apology.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!
Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Shortens to algún before masculine singular nouns (algún problema).

examples.trans: Does it have any sign on the door?
I bought some red apples.

meanings.note: Masculine noun of Greek origin despite ending in -a: el problema, algún problema.

examples.trans: Is there any problem with the shower?
We solve problems as a team.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Tener una reserva = to have a booking.

examples.trans: The reservation is here.

examples.text: Vemos las reservas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the reservations from the door.

meanings.note: Por accidente means 'by accident'.

examples.trans: The accident is here.

examples.text: Vemos los accidentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the accidents from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Plural los huéspedes.

examples.trans: The overnight guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huéspedes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the overnight guests from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Plural los hoteles.

examples.trans: The hotel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hoteles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hotels from the door.

meanings.note: Cerca de + noun = near something; de cerca = up close.

examples.trans: My family lives very nearby.
Look closely at this page.

meanings.note: La estación de tren = the train station.

examples.trans: The station is here.

examples.text: Vemos las estaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stations from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg parezco.

examples.text: Este rincón parece un jardín secreto.
examples.trans: This corner looks like a secret garden.
The idea seemed excellent to us.

meanings.note: Opposite of vacío (empty).

examples.trans: It is a full piece.

examples.text: Vaya... ¿con esta lluvia? Todos los hoteles cerca de la estación parecían llenos.
examples.trans: Oh dear... in this rain? Every hotel near the station looked full.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: ¡No se preocupe! = Do not worry!

examples.text: No te preocupes por el papeleo.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the paperwork.

examples.text: Nos preocupaba el frío de la noche.
examples.trans: We were worried about the night chill.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Estar preparado = to be ready.

examples.trans: It is a ready piece.

examples.text: ¡No se preocupe, por favor! Hemos preparado nuestra buhardilla tranquila de la tercera planta solo para usted.
examples.trans: Please do not worry! We prepared our quiet third-floor attic room just for you.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Top-floor room with sloping roof beams.

examples.trans: The attic room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las buhardillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the attic rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Shortens to tercer before masculine singular nouns (el tercer escalón).

examples.trans: It is a third piece.
Come on, race you to the third floor!

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.
The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!
